I've been around this game since it came out and still love to jump back into it from time to time to see what The Fun Pimps have added to this never ending and non stop growing game. It's sad to know what happened with their legal issues when Tell Tale Games went under but this is a testament to how dedicated this Dev team is to their work of art. Sure it needs a little elbow grease but they keep on polishing it and I really love how far this game has come since its release. Thank you.

Not to mention the zombie survival system they have to make the game always challenge you as you play in my opinion is such a good and well executed concept that personally would like to see more systems like this added to more games.

Some of the mechanics are not what you'd call intuitive, the combat is janky af, and despite the recent 1.0 release make no mistake, what you are playing is very much a decade old game.

But... Get used to all that, and you have a very fun game. I've played a lot in the survival crafting genre. I was a latecomer to 7 Days to Die, and it has quickly become one of my favorites. It's fun to play as a squad with a few buddies, the options are very customizable, and there are a LOT of good mods available, most of which are installed simply by dropping the file into the mod folder.

I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes zombies and base building

A21 ruined the game. It makes you 100% dependent on the trader, and looting. Removing jars was absolutely a keystone moment for the game. Game is now locked into one specific progression path, there is no other play style other than the one the game forces you into. Want to boil water from the local pond? Nope, you need a water filter from the trader to build a dew collector, because dew is not pure water, and boiling water collected in a container is too realistic?

Unlocked a recipe for bacon and eggs? Well, that's too bad. You have to read 9 more books before you can.

Sure A21 looks great and is heavily optimized, but what is the point if you torpedo all the foundational mechanics of a survival game? Like the freedom of play style?

Here's a funny thing that happened to me in-game a few months ago: I was camping out in the barn at the farm house and i had build a nice little storage facility upstairs and it was night and the barn was surrounded by a TON of zombies. From the place where i was standing i was safe because they couldn't attack the building. But then another player joined my server and she stood in the wrong place in my safe zone. The zombies attacked one of the major load bearing beams and the whole barn collapsed on us. I managed to escape with 10% health left. My friend did not; she was crushed and killed by the roof falling on her. All my storage chests were destroyed and their contents lost too :(

If you are looking for a fun relaxing game to play with your wife and kids, this is the perfect game. 7 Days to Die is extremely kid friendly and educational for when zombies eventually take over the world.

In most of the survival games out there, the player progression remains linear, and even if the game denies it, there is an ending. Once you become stronger than everything outside of your base, these games pass their expiration date.

There are not many games around that can conceptualize and fulfill the objectives of "Sandbox/Survival" genres as good as 7 Days to Die. the whole horde mechanic in every 7 days might seem a simple idea, but the idea itself creates a status quo between player and the game itself even if you spend a 100 hours on a game, this balance of power does not break the dedication of the player to the game by the time passes, since player progression still exists and one who was using wooden clubs might be able to craft machine guns at later phases of the game.

Implementing an "in every 7 days there will be hordes of zombies attacking your base, and as long as you play this game these zombie hordes will become stronger" to the core game loop just makes sure that the player will not be the "strongest thing out there."

I wrote a review on Alpha 8.1 stating how I didn't agree with any of the development choices, or the PR standards of The Fun Pimps.

While I'm not sure about how their PR has changed, their development processes certainly have to a very forgivable level.

They have since stopped making the game increasingly "hard," or "hardcore," and added options and features that make the game very enjoyable to anyone from casual gamers to DayZ fans.

The survival aspect of this game is fantastic for an Alpha-stage product, and they are working hard to make the graphics more and more stunning.

I can't wait to see them impliment the mocap animations on their zombies, and perhaps give their models or textures an update.

To be honest, this game IS really fun, but the random leveling is really dumb. In order to be able to craft certain items, you have to level up a specific skill to do so. The catch is, you can't progress these skills yourself by crafting certain items, or using certain tools, or anything that ANY OTHER survival RPG would have you do. You HAVE TO find randomly dropped magazines to progress these skills which is such a stupid mechanic.

Overall, it would be a really fun game but the leveling system is absolutely brain-dead. How can you call this a "survival RPG" when the game basically forces you to use items that you didn't spec in because you only find magazines for, say, sledgehammers when you wanted to use batons. Such a shame that the devs took this game in this direction because it used to be REALLY fun. It looks a lot better now, sure, but the gameplay has suffered over time.

Where to start on 7days? This game has sadly been the reason i can agree with the World Health Organisation that gaming is an addiction, with over 1500 hours in the game. I have been playing this game before it left Early Access. I loved it then and I still love it now. Many of the changes in the stable update were logical and improved the quality of life. This game has one of the most well-developed building systems I have ever seen with the ability to craft almost every block, poster, and piece of furniture in survival mode. Not only is the creativity unmatched, but the mechanic to repair and upgrade blocks is well-done and satisfying too. Constant updates to improve game quality, remove bugs, and add new and engaging content will keep you coming back.

This game truly has everything you could want from an open world survival crafting game. You can choose to collect resources (which is always so relaxing), raid POIs for high-quality loot and excitement, you can do quests for the trader and level up, and you can even complete challenges (ex: "kill 50 bears") to get more XP and sometimes rewards! Gameplay is also customizable so you can tailor the game to your needs.

Genuinely a fantastic game and perhaps one of the best survival crafting games on the market right now. I am excited to see what the devs will add/change with the new update coming in a couple months!

Summary: 7 days to die is a game that could be compared to minecraft, with less emphasis on building and more on fighting and gathering ressources. Gather stuff, craft weapons and armor, try not to die.

On that point, the game is fun: The gathering is satisfying, and the combat is fine, although it can be extremely punishing if you get infected. 7 days to die is still obviously rough around the edges though; The graphics are fine but not amazing, and the UI is kind of ugly... the amount of ressources needed for specific buildings (like the foundry) is also way overtuned. Another big sore point is how the achievements are. Clearly, they weren't thought through: I'm confident that they had to be changed midway through and now they do not make much sense. This game has been out too long for me to let go that it is still being developped: I doubt much will change to make it better. Edit: Well, I guess it's out, finally.

My friends and I love this game, it's awesome.

Update: About a hundred hours later, yep, still fun.

2026 update: It's in the best state it's ever been in. You definitely need to give this game a try.

This is a letter from a broken-hearted lover.
I have played 7 Days to Die since Alpha 11 back in April 2015 and spend about 250+ hours in the game (played a lot offline due to internet accessibility issues).
More than 3 years later, the game is still in a terribly broken state. Updates are released once in a year and cause more bugs than they solve. The sad truth about this game is that it filled a rather unique niche during the great survival game hype but the devs got lost in minor gameplay additions instead of fixing the game's major issues. I still love this game for its awesome mix of hard survival, balanced crafting and breeze of horror but the sheer confusing quantity and quality of bugs and broken gameplay mechanics really demand too much forgiveness.
Another big issue is the lack of communication from the devs. Sometimes you get lucky and receive a 30 minute-ish video of some random new gameplay mechanic or small content update, presented by a dev who is not capable of playing his own game.
I have had a lot fun with playing this game my friends, but in its current sate with the current attitude of the devs, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who doesn't enjoy being disappointed.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period mostly focus on design changes, with one saying the game was once an "open sandbox" and now forces grinding.
Other reviews object to developer conduct toward content creator JaWoodle and mention AI-generated images.

lines.F1: 7 Days to Die had a negative surge (far more negative reviews than usual, often called a review bomb), Aug 2026
lines.F2: Aug 2026: 52% positive across 962 reviews (457 negative), against a usual 83% positive and 122 negative a month
